report.summary: Checkout and gateway errors began abruptly at 16:00:00Z. Payment-service error rate jumped from about 0.2% to about 39-42%, and its logs show repeated 503 responses from the external payment provider's charges API. Checkout's 502s are the propagated result: every sampled checkout error is 'payment-service returned 502'. The payment provider's status page reports elevated Charges API errors, which points to an upstream provider outage rather than a change in our own services. Our own signals are secondary: payment-service latency rose to about 10s p99 from retries against the failing provider, and the search-service deploy at 15:40 shows no matching symptoms. Confidence is high but not verified, because we have no direct metrics or logs for the provider itself.

root_cause.mechanism: The external Charges API started returning 503s at about 16:00:00Z. payment-service retries each charge three times, which pushes p99 latency to about 10 s and trips its 'payment-provider' circuit breaker. Checkout then receives 502s from payment-service, and the gateway returns 5xx to customers.
assumptions: The status page is accurate and the outage is on the provider side.
payment-service's own health checks are shallow.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The external Charges API started returning 503s at about 16:00:00Z. payment-service retries each charge three times, which pushes p99 latency to about 10 s and trips its 'payment-provider' circuit breaker. Checkout then receives 502s from payment-service, and the gateway returns 5xx to customers.
assumptions: The status page is accurate and the outage is on the provider side.
payment-service's own health checks are shallow.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A misconfigured retry, timeout or circuit-breaker setting in payment-service turns a partial provider degradation into a full failure. The retry and wait behaviour adds about 10 s of latency and causes checkout 502s.
assumptions: Payment-service retry and breaker settings are inadequate for provider errors.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v5.3.2 ranking-model deploy at 15:40Z caused slow search-index shard responses, and this propagated to checkout. This is unlikely because the errors start at 16:00 in the payment path and search is not in checkout's dependency list.
assumptions: search-service may be a hidden dependency that is not in the dependency graph.

observed_facts.statement: checkout-service error_rate jumped from about 0.35% at 15:55:00Z to 21.17% at 16:00:00Z and stayed between 19.85% and 22.47% through 16:30:00Z.
api-gateway error_rate jumped from 0.37% at 15:55:00Z to 7.73% at 16:00:00Z, and api-gateway request_rate and CPU stayed flat.
payment-service error_rate jumped from 0.17% at 15:55:00Z to 39.13% at 16:00:00Z and peaked at 41.94% at 16:10:00Z.
payment-service latency_p99_ms rose from 464 ms at 15:55:00Z to 9857 ms at 16:00:00Z, while its CPU (about 33%), memory (about 54%) and request rate (about 59 req/s) stayed normal.
payment-service logs show 35 ERROR lines 'POST https://api.payprovider.example/v2/charges failed: 503 Service Unavailable (attempt 3/3)' starting 16:00:02Z.
checkout-service logs show 60 ERROR lines 'order # failed: payment-service returned 502 Bad Gateway' starting 16:00:27Z.
payment-service's circuit breaker for 'payment-provider' changed CLOSED -> OPEN at 16:02:04Z, 16:10:06Z, 16:17:50Z and 16:25:02Z.

The dependency health check reports payment-provider as 'degraded' with the status page message 'Elevated error rates on Charges API (investigating)'; payment-service, payments-db and checkout-service health checks return HTTP 200.
The only change in the window is search-service deploy v5.3.2 at 15:40:00Z. The last payment-service deploy (v3.1.3) was 2026-09-03T10:00:00Z.
search-service WARN logs show shard 3 slow responses (about 700-980 ms) at 15:32, 15:49, 15:51 and 16:05; search-service has no ERROR lines.

assumptions: The health checks are shallow and do not exercise the payment charge path or the provider's TLS and API behaviour.
The status page reflects the real provider outage and is not stale.
payment-provider has no metrics in this telemetry, so its state is known only from the status page and from payment-service's view of it.
The 16:00 onset is the same time the provider began failing, since no change of ours lines up with it.
payments-db is not involved, since its health check passes and payment-service CPU and memory are normal.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The primary fault is the external payment provider's Charges API outage, which returns 503s. payment-service then retries (3 attempts), its latency rises, and its circuit breaker opens. Checkout surfaces this as 502s, and the gateway surfaces checkout's failures as 5xx.

The search-service v5.3.2 deploy is unlikely to be the cause. Its timing does not match the 16:00 onset, its WARN logs are minor and it has no errors, and checkout and payment failures start only at 16:00.
Checkout-service and api-gateway resource saturation is not the cause. Their CPU, memory and request rate are flat across the onset, and their errors are downstream of payment-service.

remediation.action: Fail over or route payment charges to a secondary payment provider, or enable a degraded-mode 'pay later' path, while the provider's Charges API is down.
remediation.rationale: The provider outage is the root cause, and our own services cannot fix it.

remediation.action: Tune payment-service retries and timeouts so they stop amplifying load against the failing provider, and make checkout return a clear payment-pending state instead of 502.
remediation.rationale: Retries add latency (about 10 s p99) and tie up checkout threads.

remediation.action: Post a status update to customers and track affected orders for reconciliation or retry once the provider recovers.
Confirm the provider incident with the vendor and monitor their status page for recovery.
remediation.rationale: The health signal currently comes only from the status page.

remediation.action: Add provider-level metrics and deep synthetic charge checks to payment-service monitoring.
remediation.rationale: Today there is no direct provider telemetry, and health checks return 200 during the outage.

remediation.action: Review the search-service shard 3 latency under v5.3.2 separately, without tying it to this incident.
remediation.rationale: It is a minor, unrelated warning to track.

remediation.action: Add multi-provider or failover support for payments, with circuit-breaker-aware checkout behaviour.
remediation.rationale: This removes the single external dependency.

open_questions: Is the provider's Charges API outage confirmed by the vendor, and what is its estimated recovery time?
Why do payment-service's own health checks return 200 while charges fail (shallow health check)?
Is the 15:40 search-service deploy coincidental, or does it affect payment or checkout paths indirectly?
Did payment-service's retry and timeout settings allow the 9.8-10 s p99 latency and thread pool buildup?
